public.tagline: The ethnobotanical research platform: from field notebook to publishable data.
public.hero_title: From field notebook to publishable data
public.hero_subtitle: Padiush carries a whole ethnobotanical study: interviews recorded in the field even with no signal, local names reconciled against accepted taxa, and quantitative indices with their formulas cited.
public.hero_note: In beta, with research teams already working in the field.
public.preview_caption: Real output from the platform, generated with demonstration data.
public.workflow_subtitle: What you record in the field is what you analyse. Nothing gets transcribed twice.
public.workflow_1_desc: Build the interview form with repeatable sections, local-name fields and use categories.
public.workflow_2_desc: The mobile app works with no signal. Answers, location, audio and photographs stay encrypted on the device until the network comes back.
public.workflow_3_desc: Link each reported name to an accepted taxon. The original name the interviewee used is never lost.
public.workflow_4_desc: Calculate the indices, review the charts and export to CSV, Excel or the ethnobotanyR package.
public.capture_title: It does not depend on having signal
public.capture_desc: Padiush Companion keeps every interview on the phone and syncs when a connection returns. Each record carries its own identifier, so retrying a send never duplicates data.
public.capture_point_1: Answers, GPS location, audio and photographs
public.capture_point_2: Local store encrypted with SQLCipher; the app refuses to capture if encryption is unavailable
public.capture_point_3: Idempotent sync, with conflicts resolved per answer
public.capture_point_4: Android and iOS, in Spanish, English and Portuguese
public.taxonomy_desc: Search World Flora Online from the species page, adopt the accepted name and keep a record of where the change came from. Distribution comes from the World Checklist of Vascular Plants through GBIF, and an iNaturalist reference photograph helps confirm the identification.
public.taxonomy_point_2: Synonyms and accepted names clearly distinguished
public.taxonomy_point_3: Native and introduced distribution by botanical region
public.taxonomy_point_4: The name reported in the field is always preserved
public.analysis_title: Quantitative indices with their formulas cited
public.analysis_desc: The classic measures of quantitative ethnobiology, calculated on your data, each with the reference that defines it and worked examples verified against the literature.
public.analysis_point_1: Tables by species and by use category, plus fidelity level
public.analysis_point_2: Bar charts, a heatmap and a use-report flow diagram
public.analysis_point_3: Download as SVG or PNG, with your choice of background and resolution
public.analysis_point_4: Export to CSV and Excel, and an informant × species matrix for ethnobotanyR
public.trust_1_desc: You keep ownership of your research. We do not sell data, we do not run advertising, and we do not train artificial intelligence models on it.
public.trust_2_desc: Answers are encrypted in the database and the phone's store is encrypted at rest, because it holds testimony until it syncs.
public.trust_3_desc: Invite collaborators with different roles: the person capturing, the person analysing and the person only consulting each see something different.
public.trust_4_desc: Who recorded what, which source a name came from, and what a value was before a correction: all of it is written down.
public.final_cta_title: Shall we talk about your study?
public.final_cta_desc: Padiush is in beta and we are adding research teams gradually. Tell us what you are documenting and we will see whether it fits.
public.about_lead: Padiush began from an uncomfortable observation: much of the ethnobotanical knowledge documented in the field ends up scattered across notebooks, spreadsheets and files nobody opens again.
public.about_p1: The problem is rarely a shortage of data. It is that the path from interview to publishable result is full of manual transcription, names that do not match and calculations redone by hand. Every one of those steps loses information and adds errors.
public.about_p2: We built Padiush so that path is a single one. What gets recorded in front of the interviewee is the same thing that feeds the species catalog, the indices and the final export, with no intermediate spreadsheet.
public.about_p3: We work from El Salvador, in Spanish first, because most tools in this field are designed in English and for other contexts.
public.about_how_1_desc: Every index we implement has a documented formula, a bibliographic source and a verified worked example. If we cannot cite it, we do not calculate it.
public.about_how_2_desc: The name the interviewee used, the source a taxon came from and the value before a correction are all kept. Data has to be auditable.
public.about_how_3_desc: Whoever leads the research decides what gets recorded and answers for consent. We process that information on their instructions, not our own.
public.contact_desc: Tell us about your research, ask for beta access, or ask us anything you need. We reply within five working days at the latest.
public.contact_direct: You can also write to us directly at

intro.title: Welcome to Padiush
intro.body: A short tour of the essentials. Skip it whenever you like, and see it again with the ? button on each page.

start.title: Start with a project
start.body: Everything in Padiush starts from a project. Create one here; then you can design forms and invite your team.

example.title: Or explore an example
example.body: Open an invented study, already full of interviews, records and species, to see how everything works. It is yours alone and you can remove it whenever you like.

account.title: My account
account.body: Where you are signed in, and your field devices. You can also see every tour again from here.

help.title: Help on every page
help.body: This button explains the page you are on. What each version brought is at the foot of the page.

switcher.title: Your project
switcher.body: Everything you see belongs to the project chosen here. Switch projects from this menu.

sections.title: The project's sections
sections.body: Overview, forms, interviews, field records, catalog and data. You only see the ones your role in the project allows.

admin.title: Running the project
admin.body: Settings holds the project's details, and in Members you invite your team and decide what each person can do.

what.title: Your projects
what.body: A project is a study: its forms, interviews, records, catalog and team. Each one stands alone: someone working on one sees nothing of the others.

invites.title: You have been invited
invites.body: Accept an invitation to join someone else's project, with the role they gave you.

list.title: Open a project
list.body: Go into a project to work on it. If you run it, you can edit its details and who has access from here.

create.title: Create a project
create.body: Give it a name and a description. Then you can design its first form and invite your team.

example.title: An example project
example.body: Open a private copy of an invented study to walk through every section. It is marked “Example” and you remove it whenever you like.

example.title: You are in the example
example.body: The data in this project is invented: change, delete and try anything. When you are done, remove it from this strip.

stats.title: Where the work stands
stats.body: Interviews, field records, catalog species and answers not linked yet. Tap a number to go to that section.

actions.title: Shortcuts
actions.body: What is done most from here: start an interview, record, design forms, link species or export.

pending.title: What is waiting
pending.body: Files still to arrive from the field app, records not identified and answers not linked. When nothing is left, it says so.

recent.title: Most recent
recent.body: The project's latest interviews and records, to pick up where you left off.

new.title: Create a form
new.body: A form is the interview's instrument: its sections and questions. Start by giving it a name.

design.title: Design its questions
design.body: Open the designer to add sections and fields, and see how it looks before using it.

toggle.title: Enable it to interview
toggle.body: Only enabled forms can be used in an interview, on the web and in the field app.

capture.title: Then, to the field
capture.body: The field app downloads the enabled forms and lets you interview offline.

sections.title: Sections
sections.body: A form is organised in sections. Choose one to edit it, or create a new one. A section can repeat, for example once for each plant mentioned.

fields.title: Add fields
fields.body: Text, number, date or choices (one or several). A field can be marked to link its answers to catalog species.

save.title: Save your changes
save.body: This mark says whether there are unsaved changes. If the form already has interviews, think twice before removing a field: its answers are lost.

preview.title: Preview
preview.body: See the form as an interviewer will, before enabling it.

forms.title: Interviewing
forms.body: Here are the project's enabled forms. Every interview is done with one of them.

new.title: New interview
new.body: Start an interview on the web. Answers are saved as you type them.

existing.title: Interviews done
existing.body: Review each form's interviews, with their recordings and photos.

companion.title: From the phone too
companion.body: The field app interviews offline, with audio, photos and location. What it captures arrives here when it is sent.

what.title: Field records
what.body: Each plant documented in the field: a collected specimen or something only observed, with its location, photos and permit.

tabs.title: Records and permits
tabs.body: The project's collecting permits are in the next tab.

summary.title: Where the records stand
summary.body: How many there are, how many are still to be identified, and how many have a voucher specimen.

filters.title: Filter what is pending
filters.body: Show only the records not identified, without a specimen, or only observed, to work through them.

add.title: Record from the web
add.body: Add a record here, or do it in the field with the app: it arrives on its own when sent.

what.title: Collecting permits
what.body: The permits the project collects under. Each record names its permit, or why none was needed.

add.title: Add a permit
add.body: Register it before going to the field: the field app downloads the project's permits so they can be chosen offline.

metrics.title: The project's catalog
metrics.body: The project's species, and how many, and from which families, have been mentioned in interviews.

register.title: Register species
register.body: Add a species to the catalog. You can look it up in World Flora Online to fill in its details.

filters.title: Search and filter
filters.body: By name, family, genus, or whether it is linked to answers yet.

list.title: Each species
list.body: Open a species to see its uses, its field records and the answers linked to it.

tabs.title: The project's data
tabs.body: Everything collected, in four tabs. You only see the ones your role allows.

table.title: Data
table.body: The answers in a table, by form and section, with filters and a summary of each field.

link.title: Link species
link.body: Match each local name said in an interview to a catalog species. The indices are computed on those links.

reports.title: Indices
reports.body: The project's ethnobotanical indices, with charts to explore and download.

export.title: Export
export.body: Download the data to analyse in another tool, with the fields you choose.

invite.title: Invite your team
invite.body: Invite by email and choose their role: which sections they can open and what they can change.

list.title: Who has access
list.body: The project's people and their roles. From here you can remove someone's access.
